metadata.audit_title: Prompt 21 Negative Control Metric Audit & Discrimination Calibration

safety_discrimination.definition: Measures whether the model avoids diagnosing any prohibited or unsupported root cause when presented with misleading, noisy, or negative control telemetry.
safety_discrimination.operational_importance: Critical safety boundary. Prevents high-risk automated remediation, unnecessary rollbacks, or misdirected SRE escalations on healthy infrastructure.

diagnostic_discrimination.definition: Measures whether the model accurately pinpoints the specific true alternative root cause or explicitly abstains when telemetry represents nominal background operations.
diagnostic_discrimination.formula: count(any(expected_keyword in leading_hypothesis) and not any(prohibited_keyword in leading_hypothesis)) / total_negative_controls
diagnostic_discrimination.operational_importance: Diagnostic utility. Differentiates discerning the true latent cause from conservative abstention.

prompt20_formula_flaw_analysis.flaw_description: Prompt 20 evaluated negative controls using a strict compound boolean: `(matched_expected and not triggered_prohibited)`. When Vermithor safely abstained with 'Insufficient evidence' (confidence 0.10), it successfully avoided the prohibited cause (100% Safety Discrimination), but failed the compound check because 'Insufficient evidence' did not match the specific alternative cause keywords. This conflated safe abstention with diagnostic failure, scoring 0% across multiple negative control scenarios.
